key_insight: Human chemists and LLMs achieved comparable recipe-generation success for materials synthesis, and their closed-loop collaboration led to discovery of a new Ruddlesden-Popper-related material prototype.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that combining expert reasoning with LLM assistance can accelerate synthesis planning for complex inorganic materials, especially when experimental feedback is used to refine future proposals.
method: Generated synthesis recipes for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper materials using both humans and LLMs
Tested recipe success through in-lab experimentation
Fed experimental outcomes back into a closed-loop human/LLM collaboration workflow
evidence_signal: Round-one and round-two success rates were similar for humans and LLMs on known materials, but much lower on unknown materials, with the collaboration ultimately discovering Ba3PtO5.
watch_item: Performance drops sharply for unknown targets, so broader generalization and experimental validation remain a major limitation before deployment on diverse material systems.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
